name: Basilisk, Cyrene
body:
Cyrene CR
2

This small serpent has glossy black and green scales and curled horns flanking its fang-mouthed head.

XP 600
N Small magical beast
Init +5; Senses darkvision, low-light vision, scent.; Perception +4; Aura poisonous vapors (20 ft)

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 12, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 25 (3d10+9)
Fort +6 Ref +4 Will +1
Defensive Abilities corrosive blood; Immune acid

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +4 (1d4-2 plus poison)

STATISTICS

Str 7, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 2, Wis 11, Cha 7
Base Atk +3; CMB +0; CMD 12 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Weapon Finesse, Improved Initiative
Skills Acrobatics +5, Perception +4, Stealth +9; Racial Modifiers Stealth +4
Languages –

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Corrosive Blood (Ex)

A cyrene basilisk’s blood is highly caustic. Every time the cyrene basilisk is damaged by a piercing or slashing weapon, the attacking creature takes 1d4 acid damage (or double damage if the attack is a critical hit). Using a reach weapon does not endanger the attacker in this way.

Poisonous Vapors (Su)

At the start of a cyrene basilisk’s turn, all creatures within 20 feet take 1 point of Constitution damage (DC 13 Fort negates).

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 11; frequency 1/round for 2 rounds; initial effect 1 Con; secondary effect unconscious 1d4+1 rounds; cure 1 save.

ECOLOGY

Environment any temperate or warm
Organization solitary, pair, or nest (3-8)
Treasure none

Cyrenes are black-scaled serpents that glide through the undergrowth, plants withering and yellowing in their wake.

At first, it might be mistaken for a common grass snake.

However, it travels with its head raised, like a cobra, rather than on the ground like a grass snake. It also has distinctive white markings on its head resembling a ring or crown. Its aggressive and poisonous nature quickly dispels any notion of it being harmless. A common mistake made, given its name, is that creatures die when meeting its deadly gaze. In fact, it is the very air around the cyrene that is dangerous, as the creature releases unseen, poisonous vapors into the air around it, but it is true that the mystical gaze of the cyrene’s lambent eyes focused and intensify the pernicious poison that surrounds it like a cloak.

Every part of a cyrene is toxic, from its venomous fangs to its shimmering scales. Plants coming into contact with the basilisk as it travels wither and die in its wake, making the trail of the basilisk easy to follow. Likewise, a cyrene’s lair is marked by surroundings wasted and dead from constant exposure to the creature. The poisons leached into the soil from extended stays in its lair kill all life nearby.

The first basilisk of this kind was created by a sinister wizard from an ancient city. He created a creature so foul that it was deadly to all life it touched. For this and other atrocities, the wizard was eventually killed and all record of his name erased from history. His worst creation is remembered only by his city of origin, long since cast into ruin.
